podcast.title: Amicable Departure of Drummer
podcast.body: Hugh Whitaker stayed with the group for one album before amicably departing for other opportunities. He went on to play with other bands like The Servants. "He stayed with the group for one album before amicably departing for other opportunities."

podcast.title: Hugh Whitaker Gasoline, Firebombing, and Axe Attack on Former Business Partner
podcast.body: After the House Martins broke up, drummer Hugh Whitaker invested his life savings with a partner named James Hughitt in a car dealership. By 1993, Hughitt's mismanagement had left Whitaker completely broke. Whitaker responded by pouring gasoline into Hughitt's mailbox at least twice; when this produced no results, he firebombed his house; when that also failed, he attacked him with an axe, hacking him up significantly. Whitaker served a six-year sentence for assault. He now plays in local bands in Leeds and stays away from the car business. Meanwhile, another House Martins alumnus, guitarist Quentin Cook, renamed himself Fatboy Slim and sold a billion records. "He went a little crazy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Indie Pop Band of the 1980s
podcast.body: The Housemartins were described as a "nice tight English Indy pop band from the 1980s," notably featuring Norman Cook (later Fatboy Slim) as their bassist before his foray into dance music. "Norman Cook used to be the bass player for the House Martins, a nice tight English Indy pop band from the 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Evolution from The Housemartins
xref.body: The Beautiful South evolved from the indie band The Housemartins. It was described as another lovely pop band. "Another lovely pop band."

xref.title: Transition from Indie Pop to Dance Music
xref.body: Norman Cook, formerly the bass player for the "nice tight English Indy pop band" The Housemartins in the 1980s, transitioned into producing dance music, adopting the moniker Fatboy Slim by 1996. "Norman Cook used to be the bass player for the House Martins, a nice tight English Indy pop band from the 1980s."
